raw_response:
I've been on this 8 mu ever since I married into this village, thirty years now. My husband's down in Handan most of the year doing construction work — he only comes back for the busy times. My son and his wife live in town too. So day to day it's mostly me in the field, and my daughter-in-law helps when she's home.

This is cotton country. Everyone around here grows cotton, so that's what I know best. But I always keep a little maize and some mungbean too — you can't eat cotton, and prices go up and down. Better to have some of our own food in the house.

So this year, same as most years — about **5 mu cotton, 2 mu maize, 1 mu mungbean**. That's what I decided and that's what I'll do.

**Cotton (5 mu).** I'll plant around the 20th of April, when everyone in the village goes out. I buy the Bt seed at the agro shop in town — Old Wang next door uses the same kind and his cotton is always good. Costs about 50 yuan a mu for seed. I lay plastic mulch first then plant through it, that's how we do it now, saves water and keeps the weeds down.

For fertilizer I put down 2 bags of compound (the 15-15-15) before planting, that's 80 kg a mu. Then when the cotton starts squaring I topdress with about 10 kg of urea. Same as last year. My cousin tried to save money one year and only used 1 bag — his cotton came up yellow and skinny, didn't get half the yield. I'm not making that mistake.

Irrigation I do twice — once at squaring, once when bolls are filling. The well water is metered now, it's not cheap. If it rains good at the right time I'll skip one.

I spray herbicide once before planting, then for insects aphids twice and whitefly once usually. Bt takes care of the bollworm mostly.

Picking is the hard part. Cotton opens in September and I go back and forth, pick three or four times through October into early November. My daughter-in-law comes to help. If I really can't keep up at peak I might hire a neighbor lady for a few days, 100 yuan a day. Last year I got around 250 kg of lint per mu. I expect about the same.

**Maize (2 mu).** Spring maize, since I don't do wheat. Plant early-mid April, harvest in August. This is for us — flour for noodles and some for the pigs. One and a half bags of compound and a bit of urea, that's enough. Water once at tasseling if it's been dry. Usually get 400 kg or so a mu.

**Mungbean (1 mu).** I save seed from last year, don't need to buy. Plant in June when it warms up properly, harvest in September. Put down half a bag of compound, that's all — mungbean doesn't need much, our old people always said it makes its own food somehow. No irrigation, it's a tough plant. Get 90-100 kg a mu. Most I keep for the family — we cook mungbean soup all summer when it's hot — and sell a bit at the village market.

Altogether I'm spending maybe 2,800 yuan on inputs. That's about what I can manage. Anything left over I put aside for emergencies — you never know when someone gets sick or the well pump breaks.
